item.title: CuTe
item.description:
The Problem
GPU tensor operations require mapping logical coordinates (rows, columns, tiles) to physical memory offsets. The mapping is non-trivial: layouts can be nested, swizzled, or composed from multiple strides. C++ CuTe solves this for CUDA kernels, but prototyping layout transformations requires compiling CUDA code, which is slow and excludes non-GPU environments. Developers need a way to experiment with layout algebra without the CUDA toolchain.
What This Does

item.title: HiLS Attention
item.description:
The Problem
Long-context language models face a fundamental efficiency wall. Full attention scales quadratically with sequence length, making 100K+ token contexts prohibitively expensive for both training and inference. Existing sparse attention methods either require hand-crafted selection rules that miss important tokens, or cannot be trained end-to-end under the language modeling loss, limiting their effectiveness on real tasks.

item.title: Flowise
item.description:

Building production AI agents typically requires stitching together multiple LLM providers, vector databases, and tool integrations through custom code. Teams waste time on boilerplate integration logic rather than agent behavior. Flowise addresses this by providing a visual node-based editor where users construct agent workflows without writing backend glue code.

item.title: quill
item.description:
The Problem
macOS has no built-in way to record both microphone and system audio during a video call, then automatically transcribe the result locally. Existing tools either send audio to cloud APIs, require virtual audio devices, or bundle heavy Electron apps for what should be a menu-bar utility.
What This Does
Quill is a single Swift binary that sits in the menu bar. One click starts recording two separate .caf tracks—your mic and all system audio—using Core Audio process taps (macOS 15+)....
